developer_description: AION 2 is the only MMORPG built around a world where the sky is the battlefield. Choose your faction, ascend as a Daeva, and fight a faction war across a world 36 times larger than the original. PC only, on Unreal Engine 5.

reviews.text: Make sure you create an NCSoft Purple account BEFORE you start up the AION 2 game in steam if you are wanting to link the two accounts (especially if wanting it for the Twitch drops). There is currently a problem where if you load the steam game first then try to link the account it will tell you that you can't as one already exists. If you do a work around and delete the steam account version it will wipe everything you purchased and progress made with any charas as well as the charas. The devs have said they are looking into it. If you have already done it in the wrong order (like I did lol) then it is up to you if it is worth it to lose the charas, etc and possibly have issues or just sit and wait it out (what I am doing). Up to you, but I just wanted to warn people so they can hopefully see this before they do stuff in the wrong order. I had an issue where my onscreen UI would disappear and I could hear it responding to key binds, but could not see them. I was baffled at first, but did figure out what was going on. So when I take screenshots in games it uses Steam's overlay and the keybind F12. In Aion2 the hide/unhide UI (for taking beautiful screenshots without the UI and name tags, etc in it) is coded by default as F12. I changed the AION2 keybind to F10 and it isn't an issue anymore. Hope this helps someone else if they run into this issue of conflicting binds. To switch quickly between Aion2 combat (and movement/camera control) and Aion1's combat (and movement/camera control) just hit / It will teach you this in the tutorial, but just know you can switch back and forth like crazy and is honestly a very nice perk. Lore wise this game takes place after the original Aion game. The Balaur dragonlords won the war and Daeavas are by and large prisoners and batteries. The opening scene introduces a team of Elyos Daeva NPCs (regardless of whether you play as Asmodian or Elyos) and after a very short stint where you control one of the NPCs to move the story along and learn rudimentary controls and combat, you are rescued by said NPC daeva and rolled into the character creation screen. From there you will control your character. The initial town area for some of the intro quests/storyline will flash the screen blue and make you in a separate ... not instance, but other players are not visible, which is nice as it allows you to do required entry level quest intros without having to worry that someone else will trigger the sequence before you and cause you to have to wait or restart. I think that was well handled. When it is over it will flash blue again and other players and mobs will reappear. In the beginner area the required mobs auto repopulate VERY quickly, again this is super nice with the load of people joining all at once so you aren't stuck in the beginner area competing to get mobs for quests. You will get your wings (and therefore access to flying and gliding) very quickly compared to the first game. Game is visually stunning. I added my PC specs as this is a laptop and a bit older. I am running everything on the auto defaults it recommended for me (which is normal to low for everything). I don't have any complaints and haven't had issues other than potentially lag or loading related ones when being teleported to another area (which is fairly normal for me, your mileage however may vary). For money related things. There will be an optional subscription for the game which gives access to the marketplace. You can play without a sub (true free to play playing). There apparently is two different forms of the battlepass. From what I understand it accelerates progress, etc, but isn't required ( I will update this if I find out it is required for something). There is a skin/cosmetic shop. Not a ton in it currently, but probably they will add more later. There are some nice looking stuff in there. There are different tabs of skin types. Some are sets, some are individual items. The sets can be mixed and matched for pieces. Pets (both those purchased and those tamed from wild beasts) are also supposed to be mounts as well... which will make for some odd screenshots depending on the pet/mount type. Devs have said that Oct 14th they will allows moving around from servers to servers so people can get together who were separated by servers being full up when EA launched. I don't know if it will have strings attached (special rules) for hoping around, you should watch for more official news announcements from the dev team to be sure what is going on. I genuinely like this game so far. I also played Aion1 from launch for several years so I am somewhat biased. I am just playing and having fun, not trying to speedrun it to end game content so my review and views are based on that outlook.

Rampant market manipulation and predatory scalping are destroying progression. Absolute nightmare experiencing the current marketplace ecosystem. The lack of guardrails against blatant hoarding and predatory marketing tactics is completely ruining player progression. Recently, a scalper bought out the entire supply of Wrathful Will at 500k and maliciously relisted them at a ridiculous 1.6m... don't forget we pay $15.00 USD a month just to get access to a gatekept and manipulated market! The player(s) deliberately timed the buyout RIGHT when abyss bosses spawned so nobody would notice in real-time. Premeditated manipulation instantly inflated the crafting cost of EVERYONE'S weapon & armor by a minimum of 1/4th crafting cost, added on top.

Fun if you know what you're getting yourself into. It's a Korean MMO, so there is P2W. With that said its mainly a PvE focused game with a lot of the PvP being either equalised in some modes or restricted into to power categories in others (abyss). Besides that it is a fun

type of game with a heavy focus in both vertical and horizontal progression (literaly everything you do counts towards your total power), for example just killing a cool looking mob will unlock it as a mount and also give you permanent stats if you kill it x number of times. Combat is pretty simple on all classes, and all classes are equally

, which allows you to really just play whatever is cool aesthetically. The main difficulty in the game comes from the higher end dungeons/raids that have pretty crazy mechanics later on which makes you grateful your class doesnt require giga sweat actions per minute. Character customization is really good, you can spend hours in it. Another nice thing is gear you

becomes account wide cosmetics, so eventually you will sit on a bunch of different, free cosmetics you can mix and match. The only important and most likely cause of people not adopting the game would be the monthly subscription model it has, which allows access to marketplace (sell and buy stuff), gives 2x dungeons drops (using 2x the energy) and a bunch of other QOL stuff. It will feel really painful to play completely F2P without this active. But if you're happy with progressing slower and being

mode its not really an issue - unless you're aiming for the top 10%. A lucky F2P can technically be on par with most of the casual subscription users, albeit it unlikely. Its also possible to earn the premium currency in game via the market, which is what I did and made about $60 worth of premium currency on the first few days of launch. It really is a marathon and not a sprint type of game. So the best tip you can get would be to just do whatever is fun in the game, dont overoptimise and min max sweat if you dont want to.

I uninstalled last night. I am free to play and I grinded very hard 136 hours since its release, just to craft the weapon of my dreams and it failed... I do not understand how this game works if I am blacksmithing professional level 50 (max level) and still fail and lose all my hard earned materials in an instant. As a free to play I will not be able to get back this opportunity so I just uninstalled, cuz what's the point. It feels like a tactic to get me to take my credit card and rage spend in an instant to get what I worked for for these past weeks. nice try! worst game.

If you looked at this game and thought 'wow this looks like some of the most generic korean mmo slop I've ever seen', CONGRATULATIONS! You're right! I genuinely only recommend this game if you don't want to play it long term. Every korean mmo is exactly the same, Digimon Masters Online taught me a lot about how the Koreans think, so here's the rundown: In Korea a game isn't made

, a game is a project, it's a hobby, it's a flex. You slave away at your real job so you can INVEST in your fake life to have a better account than the kimchi connoiseur next to you on the train. They make the game to form an addiction, and this results in lazy, uninspired choices to waste your time and of course your money. They are careful about it though, they want to make you feel like you can make progress easily just by playing, but the paywall always looms hidden in the treeline, waiting to strike. They also just LOVE gambling, period. Ever wanted to gamble on an arbitrary number that determines the power of a piece of gear? You're in luck! That's what ALL these games do. I could go on. So why recommend if I think it's just a glorified scam? Well... 1a. The character creator is fun to work with, one of the best I've ever used 1b. The boob slider actually does something, western devs would call HR crying hysterically 2. I like flying around it controls a lot better than I expected I guess that's not much but hey it's a fun enough game when you go into it resolved to spend 0$.

Basically Black Desert but less complicated and kinda soulless. It's still fun if you enjoy grinding and you are into character customization. However it get's a thumb down for the Long-Term Inactive Account Policy. I can't dedicate my life to a game and if they delete your character after being inactive for more than 6 months then they can stick it where the sun don't shine.

It's pretty good as a themepark MMO. I could see myself playing this for a couple of months. With that said, the game comes with a myriad of issues, such as: 1. Aggressive monetisation 2. Outfits are not account wide 3. Bad ping from OCE 4. Movements feel kinda floaty 5. Solo dungeons are tedious 6. level scaling 7. Too many systems affecting your stats like achievements, etc. I would only recommend it if you like BDO and FF14 or maybe you just wanna play a game with hot b*tches.

Not recommended. Pretty wings, ugly systems. I put 100 hours into AION 2 after buying Early Access. I wanted this to be good. Early game is actually fun The world looks great and flying feels excellent. It’s properly integrated into exploration and combat instead of being a gimmick. Combat feels satisfying at first. Skills unlock, combos feel good, the fantasy of being a Daeva soaring around is strong. Character customization is solid. The game does a good job of making you want to keep playing through the early levels. For a while it genuinely feels like a modern, prettier Aion. Then you hit the wall Around level 45 and roughly 1500 gear score the real mid-to-endgame starts, and the game turns into a pure resource/RNG treadmill. The entire content structure is just gear score gates: Get to ~1000 GS → first difficulty dungeons Push to 1400 GS → next tier Then 1600 Then 2100 Actual 10-man endgame PvE raids are locked behind a 2800 gear score requirement What in the absolute f*ck. At that point progression stops being about playing the game and becomes about pouring time and materials into gear that is mostly gambling: Crafting has real failure chance that eats your materials Dungeon drops are not reliable Substats go through multiple layers of Soul Binding / Sync / Reset RNG Getting proper rolls feels practically impossible without burning massive resources The blatant cash grab They advertise “no P2W” and the cash shop is full of skins. Meanwhile: You can buy premium currency and convert it straight into Kina through the exchange That Kina buys materials and gear on the market The entire player market/auction house is locked behind the $15/month membership Membership also raises your Odyle Energy cap from 560 to 840 so you can actually farm the dungeons that matter Energy recharges stupidly slowly. When the sub expires you’re left with almost nothing Without paying you’re limited in almost every system that actually matters for progression. Combat becomes braindead The long-term combat plan is basically: level to 21, unlock most skills, optimize a macro, then hold two mouse buttons forever. The macro works, but it removes any real decision-making. You stop thinking and just blast. It gets boring fast. Extra insult There’s still a policy that lets them delete characters after 6 months of inactivity. They claim they don’t plan to use it, but the rule is sitting there. And Early Access characters can only transfer to other Early Access servers in the first window, so I can’t even bring my progressed characters over to play properly with friends who started on free launch servers. Final thoughts Early game is engaging and the fantasy is strong. Once the gear score gates and multi-layer RNG kick in, the game reveals itself as a polished cash-grab treadmill designed to make you either grind forever or open your wallet. I can’t justify putting any more time into it. Beautiful on the surface. Predatory underneath. I’m done. NCSoft can rot in hell. They are a vile company.
